messages:
Maya: Heads up — security scanner flagged CVE-2024-4271 in node-yaml at build time, transitive via our build tooling. Potential prototype pollution vulnerability in YAML parsing. Tagging for triage.

Jon: @Maya can you paste the vuln summary + likely attack path?

Maya: Summary: 'Prototype pollution in node-yaml <=1.2.3 allows an attacker to set __proto__ during parse. Impact: CI manifests parsed by our runners may allow object injection. If attacker can influence a parsed YAML (e.g., via PR or package metadata), they might manipulate process env or attacker-controlled inputs to the runner. This could lead to leakage of secrets available to the runner (service tokens used to call KMS or vault).'

Priya: Severity/Exploitability? Public proof-of-concept?

Devon: NVD CVSS ~7.5, PoC published on GH yesterday. Exploit requires ability to submit YAML that our CI will parse (PRs, package manifests). Public exploit exists so we should treat as high for workflows that accept untrusted YAML.

Jon: Customer impact analysis: Hosted API customers shouldn't be directly exposed unless they have CI integrations where secrets live in runner env. Dedicated & Private customers who use our CI connectors or host runners are higher risk. Also concerned about repos that allow PRs from forks.

Sophie: Mitigation options: 1) Patch build images to bump node-yaml to 1.2.4+ (quick). 2) Disable auto-run for PRs from forks. 3) Force sandboxed parsing or denylist problematic fields. 4) Rotate CI service tokens in vault as precaution. Do we do emergency rotation?

Maya: Proposed plan:
- Immediate: hotfix build images to use safe yaml (non-prod) within next 3h and run canary on a small pool of runners.
- Short-term (24h): rotate CI service tokens for teams with runner-access to customer secrets; disable PR-from-fork triggers for public repos.
- Rollout: rolling production patch window tonight 02:00–05:00 PT (minimal build disruption expected).
- Communications: notify Dedicated/Private customers with CI integrations and offer assisted token rotation.

Jon: SLA impact: no planned downtime, canary may slow builds by ~10–20%. For enterprise SLAs we should offer hands-on support. Ops: @oncall-ops please confirm window and any blackout constraints.

InfraBot: deploy job queued: canary-build-image-update -> runners-group-2, scheduled start 2024-08-26T02:15:00Z (job id infra-9832).

Devon: I'll own the hotfix and canary rollout. Priya will own token rotation + customer comms. Sophie can draft KB and mitigation steps. I'll post a short runbook for canary checks.

Priya: Draft of customer note: short, clear, no jargon. Call out: what happened, what we did (patched build images, rotated tokens for affected customers on request), recommended actions (rotate any CI keys, restrict PR triggers from forks). Will ping channel with draft in 30m.

Jon: Decision: prioritize remediation for Dedicated & Private customers with CI integration as P0. Hosted customers without CI secrets = P2. Patch window approved. Add to incident log and link to postmortem if escalates.

Maya: Adding incident ticket and tagging on-call. Will update timeline as canary results come in.

Sophie: Quick sanity check note: also search infra for any YAML parse hooks that run outside CI (deploy config parsers) — I'll scan and report in 45m.

Maya: Thanks — good catch everyone.
